requirements.statement: A file may be up to 50MB (50,000,000 bytes): the size bullet says 50MB, the browser and server checks allow it, the route's payload cap is the limit plus 1KiB, and a larger file shows 'The selected file must be smaller than 50MB'. requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 states 50MB, and DR1's inc-138 judged the same change. The backend already accepts 50MB. The frontend was put back to 10MB only because CDP's nginx ingress caps request bodies at 10 MiB; a configurable limit was rejected by DR1 because it gives no parity anywhere. Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling keeps this change blocked on the CDP ingress body cap, tracked by EUDPA-518.

requirements.blockedBy: CDP raises the nginx ingress request-body cap in front of trade-imports-animals-frontend to at least 50,001,024 bytes, and the service team records the confirmation against EUDPA-518, before this is deployed.

requirements.statement: Every file is really virus scanned. A file the scan rejects shows a red 'Virus found' tag, has no View file link, and raises '<filename> contains a virus. Remove it and try again with a different file.' in the error summary, linked to the documents table, on every view until it is removed; Save and continue holds while it is listed. A status the service cannot read shows a grey 'Unknown' tag.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 simulates a scan that always passes, so it has no failure state. A real scan can find a virus: a real constraint the prototype cannot express, so the real failure handling stays.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-075 and trace-e2e-p12-037 show the Virus found state and its error today.

requirements.statement: While a document is scanning, the page updates its status without the trader acting: with JavaScript it polls a JSON status endpoint every 3 seconds up to 10 times, updates settled rows in place, announces 'Document scan complete: the file is safe to use' or 'Document scan failed: a virus was found. Remove the file and try again.' in a polite live region, and redraws from the server once every scan settles; without JavaScript a 'Refresh virus scan status' link re-reads the status; after 10 attempts the hint 'Still checking some documents. Refresh again in a moment.' shows.
requirements.why: A real scan takes time; the trader needs to see it finish. Design Release 2.1 fakes this with a timed call, which the real scan replaces.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-097 to repo-frontend-p8-101 and trace-e2e-p12-048 show polling, announcements and the no-JavaScript refresh link today.

requirements.statement: A document that scanned clean has a 'View file' link (hidden text 'for document N') that downloads the stored file byte for byte through the service, with the file's own content type only when it is an accepted type, nosniff and the other security headers; a pending or rejected file has no link, and another notification's upload is answered 404.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 never stores a file, so it cannot show one; storing and serving the real file is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express, and the trader needs to check what they attached.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-064 and trace-e2e-p12-052 offer and serve View file for clean documents today.

requirements.statement: Each row has a 'Remove' button styled as a link, usable while the document is still scanning; it removes the document straight away with no confirmation, deletes its upload, discards anything typed in the form and reloads the page. requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-066 and trace-animals-fit-p22-058 remove a document at once with no confirmation today.

requirements.statement: Each Remove button (and View file link) carries visually hidden text naming which document it acts on ('document N').

requirements.deltaNote: Today Remove carries hidden text 'document N' (repo-frontend-p8-065).

requirements.statement: Uploading documents is optional: with no document type chosen, Save and continue moves on without any error and anything else typed is discarded; with a type chosen but other fields blank, the trader is held on the page with the missing-field errors and the chosen type stays selected.
requirements.why: The design and the real page agree: the type is the one field a trader cannot fill by accident, so it marks a document on its way.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-079 and repo-frontend-p8-081 skip an untouched form and hold a type-only form today.

requirements.statement: Save and continue with a document type chosen and every field valid saves the document and moves the trader on at once; documents still being scanned do not hold them, and the 'You cannot continue until all documents have been scanned or removed' error goes. Only a document the scan rejected holds Save and continue.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 saves and moves on, and lets the trader continue while a document is still 'Scanning for virus'. Waiting for the scan on this page is a design choice, not a constraint: the backend only publishes documents that scanned clean.
requirements.deltaNote: Today Save and continue with a document saves it and returns the trader to the page (repo-frontend-p8-080), and any document not yet scanned clean holds them with 'You cannot continue until all documents have been scanned or removed' (repo-frontend-p8-076).

requirements.statement: Save and continue goes to the next journey step, Consignment addresses (roles and addresses); when the page was opened from the overview it returns to the overview, and from the review page (or while amending, or from a template review) it returns there.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts Upload documents after the transporter and before Consignment addresses, and returns the trader to wherever they came from; the real page always goes to the overview. Sam's 9 October ruling confirms a page opened from its overview task returns to the overview on Save and continue (claim 39), without a ?from=hub marker (c-237).
requirements.deltaNote: Today Save and continue always leaves for the overview (trace-animals-fit-p22-064, trace-animals-fit-p23-018).

requirements.statement: Save and return to overview treats a form with a document type chosen as a document to add: it checks every field, holds the trader on the page with the errors if any fail, and otherwise saves the document before returning to the overview (or to the review page when amending). With no type chosen it goes straight to the overview.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 applies the same optional-upload check before leaving; the real page leaves at once and drops a part-filled document.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the exit to the overview always leaves and discards any part-filled document form (repo-frontend-p8-082).

requirements.statement: The page ends with a primary 'Save and continue' button, a secondary 'Save and return to overview' button and a 'Cancel and return to overview' link that goes to the overview without saving the form.
requirements.why: The design and the real page agree on the page actions.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-animals-fit-p22-034 and trace-animals-fit-p22-036 show the same buttons and link today.

requirements.statement: The page keeps where the trader came from across its own reloads (Save and add another, Remove, a validation error): opened from the overview, its Back link and Save and continue still return to the overview; opened from the review page, or while amending a submitted notification, they still return to the review page. The return context is carried by the service's own mechanisms (the live flow's fallback to the overview, and the existing ?change=1 for review); no ?from=hub or ?from=review marker and no hidden 'from' field is added.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 returns the trader to where they started however often the page reloads, and that is the behaviour kept. How the context travels is architecture: Sam's 9 October ruling says no ?from=hub marker is added and only the live flow's fallback changes (claim 39), and query parameter and form field names are the service's (claim 17).

requirements.statement: While a trader is creating a template, Upload documents is not offered: the template journey skips the page and its overview has no Documents task to follow. No guard on the page's own address is required.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps documents out of templates, because a document belongs to one consignment, and Sam's 9 October ruling confirms a template never offers documents. The same ruling says the prototype's template URL guards are not required (claim 21; c-238).

requirements.statement: The overview's 'Upload documents' link can be followed as soon as the origin of the import is answered, before the commodity or any later section is complete.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 puts no entry guard on the page beyond answering the origin; the real overview unlocks it only after origin, commodities and commodity details are complete.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the Upload documents task is followed only once origin, commodities and commodity details are complete (trace-animals-fit-p22-001, repo-frontend-p8-002).

requirements.statement: The overview has a section '4. Documents' with one task, 'Upload documents', linking to the page; it shows 'To do' while no document has been added and 'Complete' once documents are saved.
requirements.why: The design and the real overview agree on the task and its To do state; DR2.1 does not show the state after a document is added, so the real Complete state stands.
requirements.deltaNote: trace-e2e-p12-001, trace-e2e-p12-002 and trace-animals-fit-p22-066 show the task, To do and Complete today.

requirements.statement: Each document is saved to the notification as soon as it is added, as its own record in the backend's accompanying_documents collection keyed by the notification reference, with its type code, reference, date of issue as a YYYY-MM-DD date, a UUID upload id, scan status and files; it is still listed on a fresh load, and a retried save or removal does not add or remove it twice.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 keeps documents in the session and only saves the draft on some buttons. Storing them durably is a persistence constraint the prototype cannot express.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-014, repo-tests-p3-048 and repo-tests-p3-056 show each document stored and still listed after a reload today.

requirements.statement: The file goes from the browser to the frontend, which sends it through the backend to cdp-uploader for virus scanning and storage in the documents S3 bucket; cdp-uploader reports the result to the backend's scan-result callback, matched by correlation id, and a document becomes COMPLETE only when no file was rejected (fail closed). A failure to reach or use the uploader shows 'The file could not be uploaded. Try again.'. In CDP the scan is the real cdp-uploader; on the local stack it is the stack's cdp-uploader container with a mock scan.
requirements.why: This is the real upload handshake behind the page; Design Release 2.1 sends only the filename and cannot express it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-003, repo-backend-p4-018 and repo-backend-p4-063 show the proxied cdp-uploader flow working end to end today.

requirements.statement: Documents can be added and removed whatever the notification's status, are deleted with their notification, and only documents that scanned clean are referenced in the events the backend publishes.
requirements.why: These are the cross-service rules around the document record; the design does not contradict them, and amending a notification reaches the page in DR2.1 too.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-backend-p4-078, repo-backend-p4-079 and repo-backend-p4-080 hold these rules today.

requirements.statement: The documents page stays safe and recoverable: text the trader typed is HTML-escaped in table cells; a failed delete of an upload leaves the document in place; a saved document whose type the service no longer lists raises 'One or more of your saved documents are no longer valid. Review the list before you continue.'.
requirements.why: Real-service safeguards with no design counterpart; DR2.1 does not contradict them.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-063, repo-frontend-p8-067 and repo-frontend-p8-084 hold these safeguards today.

requirements.statement: Nothing on the documents page checks that an ITAHC has been attached before the trader continues: the guidance tells them they can add it later.
requirements.why: The design and the real page agree; the ITAHC is required at arrival, not at this step.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-116: no check on the page today.

requirements.statement: The documents page has no serious or critical axe violations (WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 AA) when empty, in its error state, with the date picker open, with the guidance expanded, with a file chosen and with a saved scanned document.
requirements.why: The page must stay accessible through every change this programme makes to it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-109 to repo-frontend-p8-115 run these axe checks today.

requirements.statement: How the review page shows uploaded documents ('Document 1' with reference, type, date of issue and attachment name).
requirements.why: The documents area stops at how documents show on the review page; the review area owns it.

requirements.statement: Backend document-endpoint defects: initiating or listing uploads never checks the notification exists or its reference format; the endpoints have no per-user or per-organisation scoping; the scan callback is unauthenticated; deleting a document leaves its file in S3; a download that fails mid-stream returns a truncated 200; the list has no defined order; and the API description of the scan callback omits its 400 and 404.
requirements.why: Real problems in the backend that Design Release 2.1 says nothing about and this programme does not fix; they go to the report.

requirements.statement: The documents page's Welsh copy is a machine draft not reviewed by a translator.
requirements.why: Design Release 2.1 is English only and the programme does not take on Welsh sign-off; it goes to the report.

requirements.statement: DR1's open follow-ups on the documents page: a shared helper for ordering the error summary, a browser-environment unit-test lane for the client oversize check, and the frontend container's memory headroom under 50MB uploads (stream rather than buffer).
requirements.why: The DR1 parity backlog is not a source of requirements, and Design Release 2.1 says nothing on these. They go to the report; the memory headroom matters to whoever builds the blocked 50MB change.

requirements.statement: The documents page keeps its address at the accompanying-documents slug within the notification's journey, with its JSON scan-status route and its file download beside it; acceptance criteria assert the page by its heading and destinations, not by a literal path.
requirements.why: Sam's 9 October ruling overrules the move to upload-documents (claim 20): the prototype never decides URL paths, and no increment changes an existing real path to match it. The tests repo's page object and the k6 performance suite both open the page at this slug, so neither changes, and with the move dropped no documents row needs trade-imports-performance-tests.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p8-001 and trace-e2e-p12-003 serve the page, its /status poll and its file download under accompanying-documents today, and repo-perftests-p1-034 requests it there.

requirements.statement: The documents form keeps the service's own field names and actions: a multipart post of the file with accompanyingDocumentReference, accompanyingDocumentType and accompanyingDocumentDateOfIssue, action=add for Save and add another and action=continue for Save and continue. The prototype's field names are not copied.
requirements.why: Form field names are architecture, which the prototype never decides (Sam's 9 October ruling, claim 17). The k6 performance suite posts these names to add documents and leave the page, so changing them would break it for no visible gain.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-perftests-p1-035 and repo-perftests-p1-046 post these fields and actions to the page today.

requirements.statement: Under the k6 load model every uploaded document's virus scan settles and is not rejected, with a P99 under 60 seconds, the same allowance as upload pages; a scan still pending after 120 seconds counts as stuck. The allowance is measured against CDP's real cdp-uploader: on a local run the scan is a mock, so its timings are not CDP's.
requirements.why: A trader waits on the scan before View file appears, and the performance suite holds the service to this allowance; the documents changes in this programme must not break it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-perftests-p1-043 to repo-perftests-p1-045 assert the 120-second stuck limit and the 60-second P99 allowance today.

requirements.statement: The germinal-products set has its own documents page: a copy of the live-animals documents feature folder, taken after this programme's documents changes have landed in live-animals, served at the same slug within the germinal set's journey and behaving as every adopted documents requirement here says. It is one of the germinal set's pages, since only Additional details, CPH number and permanent address are left out of it; its end-to-end, accessibility and security specs sit under tests/animals/{e2e,a11y,security}/germinal-products/.
requirements.why: Sam's 9 October ruling makes germinal products a sibling set whose pages are copies of their live-animals feature folders, taken after the live twin is built, with journey pages at the live-animals slugs (claims 1 to 3 and 15). Duplication is the app's architecture and is never weighed as a cost.

requirements.statement: The documents rows change the animals frontend (and the animals backend) only: the high-risk plants frontend takes no part of them, because it has no Upload documents page, no Documents task on its overview, no virus scan and no document-upload service.
requirements.why: Sam's 9 October afternoon ruling has plants take a change in the same increment only where plants has the same page or behaviour, and a row with no plants equivalent leaves plants alone; the ITAHC and the animal document types are animals-only data that is never mirrored.
requirements.deltaNote: The plants frontend on origin/main has no documents feature folder under sets/high-risk-plants, and its services doc puts file attachment out of scope (plants-common-mapping-2026-10-09.json, documents theme: all six rows animals only).

conflicts.about: The documents page's path segment: upload-documents or accompanying-documents.

positions.says: c-059 is overruled: the move to upload-documents is dropped and the documents page stays at accompanying-documents.
The page is served at /upload-documents.
The page is served at the accompanying-documents slug.
The k6 suite opens the documents page at accompanying-documents.

conflicts.outcome: Sam's 9 October ruling ranks first and withdraws the earlier outcome: the prototype never decides URL paths, so the page stays at accompanying-documents (req-1822) and req-477 is out of scope. The prototype's path claim is set aside; its page content still stands.

conflicts.about: Where the Back link goes when the trader came from the review page or is amending.

positions.says: Back goes to the review page when the trader came from review or is amending.
Back always goes to the overview.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: Back returns to the review page in those cases and to the overview otherwise.

conflicts.about: Wording of the 'Animals that do not need a health certificate' row.

positions.says: 'Exporter's declaration that they are fit to travel'.
'An exporter's declaration that they are fit to travel'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the cell drops the leading 'An'.

conflicts.about: Wording of the 'Rodents imported for research purposes' row.

positions.says: 'RM39 licence and supplementary health certificate'.
'An RM39 licence and supplementary health certificate'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the cell drops the leading 'An'.

conflicts.about: Whether the Document reference field has a hint.

positions.says: The Document reference field has no hint.
The field has the hint 'For example, GBHC1234567890.'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the hint is removed.

conflicts.about: Whether the document reference has a length limit.

positions.says: A real validation constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
The only rule on the reference is that it is not blank.
A reference over 58 characters is refused.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: a stored reference needs a length limit, a validation constraint the prototype cannot express, so the 58-character limit and its message stay. The prototype's blank-reference rule still holds and is kept.

conflicts.about: Which characters a document reference may contain.

positions.says: References such as 'ITAHC-001' are accepted.
The reference may contain only letters and digits.
The k6 suite records that the backend accepts letters and digits only.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype outranks the backend and the performance suite, and nothing in the evidence shows the letters-and-digits rule protects a downstream system, so it is not a real constraint: the backend drops the pattern and accepts what the page accepts (non-blank, at most 58 characters at the page). The k6 suite's own references stay valid. Re-raise if a downstream codelist proves to need it.

conflicts.about: Whether the document type travels as the prototype's slug or the service's code.

positions.says: A cross-service constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
Option values are slugs such as 'itahc' and 'air-waybill'.
Each type is sent and received by its code, aligned with the GBN-AG set.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the code is what the backend stores and the outbound event carries, so the codes stay. The trader sees the same labels either way.

conflicts.about: The Date of issue hint example.

positions.says: 'For example, 27/3/2026'.
'For example, 12/12/2025'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the hint becomes 'For example, 27/3/2026'.

conflicts.about: Wording of the size bullet in the Attachment hint.

positions.says: 'files that are smaller than 50MB'.
'smaller than 10MB'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the bullet opens 'files that are smaller than'. The number follows the limit (c-069).

conflicts.about: The largest file a trader may attach: 50MB or 10MB.

positions.says: Files must be smaller than 50MB.
DR1 judged the same difference (inc-138): raise the limit to 50MB once the platform ingress cap allows it.
The limit is held at 10MB to stay inside CDP's 10 MiB ingress cap until EUDPA-518 raises it.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype and DR1's inc-138 both say 50MB and outrank the frontend: the limit becomes 50MB everywhere. The ingress cap is a platform change outside the programme, so the requirement is adopted with blockedBy rather than kept at 10MB.

conflicts.about: Wording of the file-type bullet in the Attachment hint.

positions.says: 'PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX'.
'a PDF, DOC, DOCX, JPEG, JPG, PNG, XLS or XLSX'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the bullet drops the leading 'a'.

conflicts.about: Whether the stated file rules (type, accept list, empty file) are enforced.

positions.says: A real validation constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
No validation checks the size, type or ZIP rules.
The file input sets no accept attribute.
A file of a type not allowed is refused with a message listing the allowed types.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the service can only accept the types it can scan and serve, so the accept list and the server-side checks stay.

conflicts.about: Whether the attachment drop zone is the prototype's bespoke markup or the GOV.UK file upload component.

positions.says: DR1 judged the same difference (inc-137): use the design system's file upload, because the requirement is the behaviour, not the bespoke classes.
The attachment is a custom drop zone with a hidden file input.
The page is built from custom app-upload-documents-card classes outside the GOV.UK file upload.
The attachment field is a custom drop zone.
The server records only the chosen file name, in a hidden attachmentFileName field.
The chosen file's name is carried in a hidden attachmentFileName field.
The GOV.UK enhanced file upload gives the drop zone, with the plain input as the no-JavaScript fallback.

conflicts.outcome: DR1's inc-137 judgement on this same difference ranks above the prototype: the GOV.UK component stays, giving the same wording and behaviour ('No file chosen', 'Choose file', 'or drop file', the file named in a live region). The bespoke markup and the filename-only hidden field are not built. The prototype's wording claims still hold and are kept.

conflicts.about: Whether the chosen file is kept after a server-side validation error.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
On an error the page keeps the reference, type, date and the attachment file name.
After a failed submit the upload control reads 'No file chosen' again.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: a browser cannot refill a file input, and the prototype only keeps a filename, so the trader chooses the file again. The prototype's claim still holds for the reference, type and date, which are kept (req on kept values), so it is not overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether the typed values survive when the server refuses an over-cap request body.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
On an error the page keeps what the trader typed.
When the server refuses an over-limit body the page is redrawn with an empty form.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the server refuses the body before reading it, so there are no values to put back; the browser-side check keeps them whenever JavaScript runs. The prototype's claim still holds for ordinary validation errors and is not overruled.

conflicts.about: Where the maximum-documents error points.

positions.says: The error is on the attachment field, linked to it.
The error links to the documents table and shows only in the summary.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the error links to the Attachment field and shows inline on it.

conflicts.about: The visually hidden heading of the documents table's last column.

positions.says: The hidden column heading is 'Action'.
The hidden column heading is 'Actions'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the hidden heading becomes 'Action'.

conflicts.about: Whether the card shows empty-state text before any document is added.

positions.says: With no saved documents, no table is shown and nothing replaces it.
The card shows 'You have not added any documents yet.'.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the empty-state line goes.

conflicts.about: Whether the virus check is real, with failure states, or the prototype's simulation that always passes.

positions.says: A real constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
The virus check has only scanning and passed; there is no failed status.
A POST to /upload-documents/virus-check/{id} marks a document passed.
The page asks the server to mark each document passed after 2.5 seconds.
Under DR2.1 the status never moves on from 'Scanning for virus'.
The prototype simulates a virus check.
A page script posts to the simulated virus-check endpoint.
The status is still 'Scanning for virus' after four seconds; the check never completes.
The real scan shows Scanning for virus, Check completed, Virus found or Unknown.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: real files are really scanned and can be rejected, which the prototype cannot express. The real scan, its Virus found and Unknown states, its virus error and its polling stay; the simulated endpoint and timer are not built. The prototype's Scanning for virus and Check completed wording is kept.

conflicts.about: Whether a saved document offers View file, which Design Release 2.1 does not show.

positions.says: A persistence constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
The prototype posts only the file name; no file is stored.
A clean document offers a View file link.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: the prototype stores no file, so it cannot show one; the real service stores it, and View file stays for clean documents. The prototype's filename-only post is not built.

conflicts.about: Whether Save and continue waits for documents to finish scanning.

positions.says: After adding a document still scanning, Save and continue moves on to roles and addresses.
Save and continue holds the trader until every document is scanned or removed.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default. Waiting on this page is not a constraint: the backend publishes only clean documents, and the prototype can express a hold but does not. Pending scans no longer hold the trader; a rejected document still does, because the prototype has no rejected state to say otherwise (c-078).

conflicts.about: Where Save and continue goes from Upload documents.

positions.says: It goes to the next step, roles and addresses, or back to the hub or review the trader came from.
It always leaves for the overview.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: Save and continue goes to Consignment addresses, or back to the overview or review page the trader came from.

conflicts.about: What Save and return to overview does with a part-filled document.

positions.says: It applies the optional-upload check and saves a type-chosen document before going to the hub.
It always leaves and discards any part-filled document form.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: a type-chosen document is checked and saved (or the errors shown) before the trader leaves.

conflicts.about: When the overview's Upload documents link can be followed.

positions.says: The hub's Upload documents link works as soon as the origin is answered.
The task is followed once origin, commodities and commodity details are complete.

conflicts.outcome: The prototype wins by default: the link can be followed once the origin is answered.

conflicts.about: Where documents are kept and how they are identified: the prototype's session list or the backend's records.

positions.says: A persistence constraint the prototype cannot express overrides it.
Saved documents are kept in the session as a list.
Only Save and return explicitly saves the draft; add, remove and continue do not.
Each document records a virus status of 'uploading' and when it was added.
Each document's id is made from the time and its position.
The date of issue is stored as the text entered.
Each document gets an id doc-<timestamp>-<n>.
No upload request to a file store or scanner is made.
Documents are stored in their own collection keyed by notification reference.

conflicts.outcome: The ruling ranks first: documents are stored durably as soon as they are added, with a UUID upload id and an ISO date, through the real upload handshake. The prototype's session list, its ids, its text date and its draft-save timing are not built.

conflicts.about: Whether 'Health certificate' stays among the document types.

positions.says: The options are ITAHC then twelve others, with no Health certificate.
DR1 does not offer Health certificate to a design-release user.
An existing ruling (EUDPA-310) offers every GBN-AG document type, Health certificate included, after DR1 held it back.

conflicts.outcome: The documents page stops offering 'Health certificate': the document type select offers, in order, Intra Trade Animal Health Certificate (ITAHC), Veterinary health certificate, Air waybill, Import permit, Letter of authority (Directive 2008/61/EC), Commercial invoice, Sea waybill, Rail waybill, Bill of lading, Catch certificate, Laboratory sampling results for aflatoxin (Reg 2019/1793), Journey log, Other, matching Design Release 2.1 and the DR1 judgement in inc-136. The prototype wins by default, DR1 judged the same difference the same way, and EUDPA-310's re-offer is a choice the frontend made, not a constraint the prototype cannot express. The change is to the frontend's options (and the fit and E2E specs that assert fourteen); the backend's DocumentType enum keeps HEALTH_CERTIFICATE so documents already saved with it still load and are still coded on the outbound event.

conflicts.about: How the documents page carries where the trader came from: the prototype's ?from=hub / ?from=review marker and hidden 'from' field, or the service's own mechanisms.

positions.says: No ?from=hub marker is added; only the live flow's fallback changes so overview-opened pages return to the overview.
The form posts with ?from=review or ?from=hub and a matching hidden 'from' field.
Opened from the overview, the form carries a hidden from=hub field and posts to upload-documents?from=hub.

conflicts.outcome: Sam's 9 October ruling ranks first: the return behaviour is kept (req-542, req-539), but no ?from= marker or hidden 'from' field is added; the live flow's fallback and the existing ?change=1 carry it. The prototype's marker claims are set aside; its claims about where the trader returns still stand.

conflicts.about: Whether opening or submitting the documents page in template mode is guarded by a redirect to the overview.

positions.says: A template never offers documents, and the prototype's template URL guards are not required.
Opening the page while creating a template redirects to the hub.
Submitting the page while creating a template redirects to the hub without saving.

conflicts.outcome: Sam's 9 October ruling ranks first: the template journey never offers Upload documents (req-543), and no guard on the page's address is built.
